items.title: Switch
items.name: Switch
items.summary: Bring any AI agent into Slack, Teams & Discord
items.description: Switch brings AI agents into the collaboration tools your team already uses. Agents join as named participants in your Slack, Teams, Discord, or Telegram channels, sharing the same context and history as your team. Connect an agent once and use it across projects. Each room carries its own context, participants, and rules. Works with Claude Code, OpenAI, Google ADK, LangChain, and more. Open source, self-hostable, running in minutes.
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt! Safi here from the team at SandboxAQ that built Switch.


Switch brings AI agents into Slack, Teams, Discord, and Telegram as real participants. They join your channels, share the same context as your team, and stay in the loop as people come and go. Open source, self-hostable, first agent in a channel in about ten minutes.


Works with Claude Code, Google ADK, LangChain, OpenAI, and more.


Would love to hear how your team is working with agents today. Ask us anything!
Looks interesting. How long did it take to figure out the right apprpach for making switching between tasks easier?

Our agents post into Telegram on timers and the thing that broke first was cadence – a four-hour lookahead meant one announced a 16:00 item at 13:10 and we stopped reading it. With 40 agents in one Slack, how do you keep people from muting the channel?

items.title: OpenMarket
items.name: OpenMarket
items.summary: Multi-agent marketplace where proof decides who wins
items.description: What if marketplaces rewarded the best product instead of the best marketing? OpenMarket (in research preview), is a multi-agent marketplace where sellers pitch, competitors challenge their claims, and independent truth agents verify the evidence as they compete to earn a buyer's sale. Here, claims don’t count just because they’re written on a product page. They have to survive scrutiny and be proven.
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt, I am Ankur, founder of M11 Labs.

What broke
The best product does not win any more. The best listing wins, and those are two completely different companies.

It used to take real time and money to write a good product page and to earn the reviews underneath it, so a good page told you something about the company behind it. Now anyone can produce all of that in an afternoon for nothing, so a good page tells you nothing at all. The brands doing it properly end up in the same group as the ones who are not.

I spent years at Amazon and Meta on exactly this problem, which is how you work out what is true when there is far too much of it for anyone to check.

Why it got personal
Cosmo, my 3 year-old golden retriever, had repeated bouts of suspected -pancreatitis, caused by poor quality food from a brand everybody knows. It is painful, it can turn serious quickly, and once a dog has had it, what you feed him is most of how you stop it coming back. We were told to move him onto natural food.

I found five products. Every one of them said natural, low fat and vet formulated. There was no honest way to tell them apart, so I chose the best packaging, which means I chose the best marketer. I got it wrong, and Cosmo could not tell me it was not working.

I had every advantage and I still could not check a claim on a bag of dog food, for a decision that genuinely mattered. I am sure I am not the only person who has felt that way.

What OpenMarket is
The world's first multi-agent marketplace with over 3 million merchants, where proof decides who wins. You say what you want. Agents acting for brands, for products and for buyers all work at once. Sellers pitch in the open, rivals challenge what they hear, and independent truth agents check every claim against the evidence as it is made. When a seller says twelve hours of battery life and the evidence says eight and a half, you watch the correction land on the claim itself.

The hard parts

  1. Running competing agents in one shared room without it collapsing into a chat log.

  2. Getting rivals to actually go after each other's weakest claims instead of politely agreeing with everything.

  3. Building truth agents quick enough to reach a verdict while the claim is still on screen, and fair enough to judge between sellers who all have a reason to exaggerate.

    That last one is a very different problem from summarising, and it is the one that matters most.

Why this is a research preview
M11 Labs builds agentic commerce experiences to show a different internet than the one we have today. OpenMarket is the first one we are putting in public and it will not be the last. Everyone else is adding AI to the shop we already had, and that shop was built for a person scrolling a grid of pictures. So we started again. It has rough edges, and it is supposed to.

Try it at openmarket.m11.ai

Start with a product you already love and see how it does. Every winner in the gallery earned its place on merit, and the leaderboard shows you which claims it had to prove to get there. It is a good feeling when something you have trusted for years turns out to deserve it, and a useful one when it does not.

All Product Hunt users who try and comment get founding credits for the M11 truth agent, launching later this year. Point it at any big purchase and it will flag the inconsistencies, the mismatches and the claims that cannot be backed, before you spend a penny.

Create a brand account with code PRODUCTHUNT90 and get complementary three months of the M11 agentic trust and intelligence platform. We will show you which of your claims fail and which ones will a customer catch first, then work with you through our pilot programme to fix them before Black Friday.

@david_mataciunas and I will be in the comments all day.
Awesome product! For sure watching where this goes
Lovely experience using openmarket. Great to see AI agents compete.

items.title: Relaticle
items.name: Relaticle
items.summary: Open-source CRM with approval-gated AI writes
items.description: Most CRMs bolt AI on. Relaticle is built agent-first: any MCP client gets 37 first-party tools over OAuth, with workspace custom fields in each agent's schema automatically. The in-app assistant is stricter: every write is a proposal showing the exact change, approved record by record. Self-host everything under AGPL, including local inference with Ollama. Free forever self-hosted; Cloud is flat per-workspace pricing, not per-seat.
top_comments: Hi Product Hunt, Manuk here. I've been building Relaticle for about two years, mostly solo. It started as a conventional open-source CRM. Then I added agents and hit a question I couldn't dodge: how much authority should each kind of client get? Read-only access was too limited to be useful. Silent writes into customer data felt wrong. I ended up with two trust levels. External MCP clients (Claude, Cursor, anything that speaks MCP) authenticate over OAuth and write directly through 37 tools, the same way an API client would. The in-app assistant works next to human users, so every write it wants becomes a proposal that shows the exact change and waits for approval. Batches are reviewed record by record: you approve or skip each one, and whatever you approved is kept. The chat client itself was rebuilt after failures I hit in real use. A rate-limited retry could delete a conversation turn. A stale stream handler could write a draft into the wrong conversation. Drafts now survive reloads, failed sends stay visible, and answers link back to the records they mention. Everything self-hosts under AGPL, including model inference with Ollama. Each workspace defines its own custom fields, and they show up in the agents' schemas automatically. One question I'm still chewing on and would genuinely like opinions on: should an in-app assistant ever get policy-based auto-approval, or should every write stay explicit?
I like the smaller recovery details here too. Keeping failed sends visibla and drafts intact after a reload sounds minor, until an assistant is working with actual CRM records.
Would love an undo trail for approved writes, not just the approve step. Excited to see where this goes!

Everyone else is adding AI to the shop we already had, and that shop was built for a person scrolling a grid of pictures. So we started again. It has rough edges, and it is supposed to.

It is a good feeling when something you have trusted for years turns out to deserve it, and a useful one when it does not.

All Product Hunt users who try and comment get founding credits for the M11 truth agent, launching later this year. Point it at any big purchase and it will flag the inconsistencies, the mismatches and the claims that cannot be backed, before you spend a penny.

Create a brand account with code PRODUCTHUNT90 and get complementary three months of the M11 agentic trust and intelligence platform. items.title: Relaticle
items.name: Relaticle
items.summary: Open-source CRM with approval-gated AI writes
items.description: Most CRMs bolt AI on. Relaticle is built agent-first: any MCP client gets 37 first-party tools over OAuth, with workspace custom fields in each agent's schema automatically. The in-app assistant is stricter: every write is a proposal showing the exact change, approved record by record. Self-host everything under AGPL, including local inference with Ollama. Free forever self-hosted; Cloud is flat per-workspace pricing, not per-seat.
top_comments: Hi Product Hunt, Manuk here. I've been building Relaticle for about two years, mostly solo. It started as a conventional open-source CRM. Then I added agents and hit a question I couldn't dodge: how much authority should each kind of client get? Read-only access was too limited to be useful. Silent writes into customer data felt wrong. I ended up with two trust levels. External MCP clients (Claude, Cursor, anything that speaks MCP) authenticate over OAuth and write directly through 37 tools, the same way an API client would. The in-app assistant works next to human users, so every write it wants becomes a proposal that shows the exact change and waits for approval. Batches are reviewed record by record: you approve or skip each one, and whatever you approved is kept. The chat client itself was rebuilt after failures I hit in real use. A rate-limited retry could delete a conversation turn. A stale stream handler could write a draft into the wrong conversation. Drafts now survive reloads, failed sends stay visible, and answers link back to the records they mention. Everything self-hosts under AGPL, including model inference with Ollama. Each workspace defines its own custom fields, and they show up in the agents' schemas automatically. One question I'm still chewing on and would genuinely like opinions on: should an in-app assistant ever get policy-based auto-approval, or should every write stay explicit?
I like the smaller recovery details here too. Keeping failed sends visibla and drafts intact after a reload sounds minor, until an assistant is working with actual CRM records.
Would love an undo trail for approved writes, not just the approve step. Excited to see where this goes!

interest_sections.title: AI 面试官
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自zhihu、GitHub，核心观察是面试双方信息严重不对等，招聘方不反馈淘汰依据、求职者则借助AI模拟或实时代答来消除黑箱，AI面试工具下一步要解决“复盘透明化”和“反作弊”之间的平衡。

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 现在招聘方普遍用“等通知”不透露落选细节，求职者只能靠社区猜测、用AI App实时提词读稿应付，或像GitHub上的spontaneousai/job-hunt-copilot那样用个人素材库自动生成定制简历和模拟面试做准备。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟进的是面向求职者的“面试风险点复盘”工具，把面试官那种当天就能判断候选人行不行的评估逻辑（如说话歧义、回答断线、知识矛盾）拆解成可修正的反馈，同时给招聘方提供识别AI代答的辅助手段。

interest_sections.title: AI 任务管理
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu，核心观察是任务管理器因功能膨胀正在失去卡死自救的初心，可靠且极简的应急响应比堆叠功能更接近真实需求。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 用户在系统卡死时最需要的是能快速调出并结束异常进程的轻量入口，而不是功能膨胀反而加剧卡顿的任务管理器

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 当前任务管理器为实时监视大量数据不断叠加图表和私有API，体量膨胀50多倍并出现幽灵进程Bug，用户无奈转向重启或命令行；工具盘点则靠自定义流程和模板（如PingCode）覆盖团队场景。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是把‘救急模式’与全功能驾驶舱分离，在低资源占用下优先响应进程终止请求，并引入异常进程识别与清理建议。

interest_sections.title: 智能旅行助手
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu、GitHub，核心是攻略与预订的割裂仍是自由行规划最大痛点，生成式 Agent 正从内容聚合走向地图化行程并试探预订衔接。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 自由行用户需要一个能把游记攻略直接转成含机酒门票预订的行程单、并避免跨平台重复填写时间地点的一站式规划工具

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 现状主要是靠马蜂窝、穷游、小红书等做攻略，再回到阿里旅行等平台按机酒门票独立频道逐项手工预订，流程断裂数据不互通；GitHub 上已有人用 Agent 做“小红书调研→交互式地图行程”的尝试，但尚未接预订闭环。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是让多智能体在攻略解析、行程生成后直接联动真实库存与价格数据，把信息查询到可下单预订的链路自动化，并利用行程中的位置热度做错峰提示。

interest_sections.title: AI 财务管家
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu，财务人群的真实痛点是从发票流水到多套系统的重复导数和处理劳动，当前方案以自动化和可视化为主，下一步更稀缺的是把AI从“帮忙结账”推向“解释经营变化并给出优化决策”。

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 当前讨论集中在用智能账务引擎自动生成凭证、自动对账和异常交易检测，再通过BI看板做可视化，代表工具如用友畅捷通、金蝶云、九数云BI，目标是实现从“数据搬运”到“战略洞察”。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是由“自动记账出表”走向“能听懂业务问题的财务分析智能体”，用自然语言交互触发跨系统取数、毛利波动归因、现金流预测和税务筹划建议，而不只是提供固定模板看板。
